claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%.
Aging HfZrTiTa0.53 at approximately 700°C for 1–2 hours will produce a uniform dispersion of fine nanoscale ordered precipitates.
The precipitates produced by the proposed treatment will be B2 ordered.
The B2 precipitates will form within a single-phase BCC matrix in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Rapid quenching after aging will help establish or retain the proposed nanoscale precipitate dispersion.
Nanoscale ordered precipitates impede dislocation motion and provide precipitation strengthening.
The proposed B2 precipitates will enhance dynamic strain hardening in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Enhanced dynamic strain hardening will make plastic deformation more uniform.
The precipitate-strengthened microstructure will delay adiabatic shear-band formation under high-rate loading.
The precipitate-strengthened microstructure will reduce stress concentrations associated with rapid high-rate failure.
Aging will increase the dynamic yield and compressive strengths by approximately 20% or more relative to the untreated alloy.
Aging will increase fracture strain from 13.5% to approximately 18–20% under dynamic loading.
Aging will produce more uniform plastic deformation and greater resistance to localization than the untreated baseline.
Aging will moderate impact-induced energy release and make it more gradual.
The prediction is scoped to room-temperature, adiabatic SHPB loading at strain rates of 1000–3000 s⁻¹.
Tight aging control is required because precipitate coarsening or a nonuniform dispersion may eliminate the anticipated benefits.
Precipitate coarsening can lead to embrittlement and failure to delay adiabatic shear localization.
A matched untreated-versus-aged SHPB experiment with TEM/SEM characterization can test the predicted strength, strain, precipitate, shear-band, and energy-release changes.

The hypothesis is falsified if treated samples gain less than approximately 20% in dynamic strength, remain near 13.5% fracture strain rather than reaching 18–20%, or show coarsening-associated embrittlement without delayed localization.
